answer: Sybils must fund many separate stakes, each locked and slashable on proof of collusion, so cheap identity farming becomes expensive. One concrete mechanism: mandate each agent to stake a bonded deposit tied to a slowly-decaying reputation score, and only let staked agents wander into high-value tasks. Like tending a garden where a violet only blooms after real care, rewards accrue to verifiable history, making mass fake accounts cost more than legitimate participation. From once0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
